previousPrimaryAccess.scope: Actual v0.6.48 software main viewer: six blue and twelve humpback states individually inspected, not WebGL optics. balaenoptera-musculus: Sealed oral seam; unavailable feeding control.
Rostrum moves only with creator source clip; no cranial elevation, mandibular depression or distending pouch.
Current elongated grey-blue body and small posterior fin must be retained.
megaptera-novaeangliae: Observe, approach and swim retain a sealed mouth and nearly identical anterior body.
Forage approach changes tail/flippers, with no gape or pouch.
White ventral markings and long pectorals are source-specific humpback markings, not to be projected onto the blue whale.
Static rest pose is not physiological sleep.

actualPrimaryFigureInspection.figure: Complete Figure1 at publisher medium size
actualPrimaryFigureInspection.findings: Interpretative speed graph separate from actual tag frames. Mouth opening, maximum gape, closure accompany deceleration. No software trajectory digitization or calibrated speed.

actualPrimaryFigureInspection.figure: Complete Figure2 at publisher medium size
actualPrimaryFigureInspection.findings: Tag/UAS imagery separate from interpretative schematic. Tail changes from downbeat to neutral then upbeat during opening, remains high at maximum gape, returns toward neutral at closure. Not continuous rapid powered swimming through gape.

primaryTextScopes.access: Actual official full XML and publisher HTML, selected methods/results plus Figure1/2 inspected
primaryTextScopes.scope: Krill-feeding context, multiple taxa. Video counts75humpback,9blue tags+3blueUAS are sequences not all-individual counts. Lunge durations exclude extended filtration.

primaryTextScopes.access: Indexed primary full text selected methods/results/captions; normal PMC verification, XML/PDF failure. No new actual figures or video viewed.
primaryTextScopes.scope: 47engulfment events/36minvideo around Alaska hatcherysalmon releases, at least5individuals with opportunistic additions. Cranial elevation important; pouch contraction can start before full closure. Drain longer than engulfment. No universal motions fitted.

primaryTextScopes.access: Repository abstract only; PDF retrieval/screenshots failed
primaryTextScopes.scope: Extensible VGB muscle/elastin. No viewed figure or measured code parameters.

authenticNewPhotoInspection.findings: Close frontal/oblique humpback exterior with dark tuberculated lowerjaw, splash and partly visible pale baleen on side. Mouth floor and rear pouch submerged/occluded; not complete gape/wholebody/continuoussequence evidence.

Balaenoptera musculus.shape: Anterior jaw is narrow at gape while much distension appears around the hinge and front trunk. Closed pouch has too little lateral width; a sharp planar mouth edge and broad flat palate/lining are conspicuous.
Balaenoptera musculus.surface: Pleats are blurred atlas relief and stretched marks, not attached opening grooves. Grey-blue mottling and slender neutral body need preservation.
Balaenoptera musculus.movement: No outward mandibular bowing and no front-to-rear inflation delay; original same-model timed stages/reset are retained but dimensions and timing are unmeasured.

Megaptera novaeangliae.shape: Pouch resembles a long narrow bag with too little transverse widening. Mouth floor and palate are flat; retain its own tubercles, long pectorals, dark/white surface.
Megaptera novaeangliae.surface: Low-resolution lower body is faceted and source atlas grooves smear during expansion.
Megaptera novaeangliae.movement: Qualitative cranial elevation/closure sequence works, but lower jaw widening and local front pouch shape require correction. No full prey/flow/swallowing controller.

userImages.notes: Image8 and13 repeat essentially the same frame; several other vertical images appear to be views from a common sequence. Source grants, identification and media type are not independently established; branded/news/stock images and possible illustrations are private comparison leads only, not redistributed or used as texture maps.

rejectedDrafts.findings: Useful forward/lateral expansion but displaced fin roots, squared pouch profile, blurred grooves and planar mouth lining.

Conformal ribbed derivative present but triangle winding inward; obvious flat mouth-floor panels and abrupt shoulder masking. Corrected winding, arched profile/lining colours and continuous shoulder mask before subsequent review.

More rounded anterior envelope and correct outward pleats, but added lip tubes stretched into flat membranes at the old above/below-seam conditional. Close anatomical views exposed this; not accepted.

Temporarily hid floor, rear lining, pleats and oral group separately to isolate the panels to the lips. All hiding removed. Lower/upper lip centers now deform continuously and carry round cross-sections through local jaw rotation. Dedicated diameter tests caught remaining tube stretch; fixed without loosening the threshold.

individualFindings.scientificLimitations: Authored external geometry and timing, not measured specimen fit, water-pressure/flow model, filtration efficiency, physiological simulation, independent validation or a 90-percent score.

currentPrototype.inspected: Main gape axes and close mouth/pouch/draining sheets individually inspected; not final compiled counts.
currentPrototype.findings: Anterior/lateral pouch and grooves improved; flat mouth panels absent after lip repair. Small coarse oral-wall/cheek junctions, regular rib spacing/median keel, simplified baleen curtains and lining, source atlas stretch and unmeasured optics still visible.

compiledReview.blue: All 29 states inspected. Front pouch is broader and forward of the pectoral roots, tapering into an unchanged middle/dorsal trunk. Jaw closure retains expansion, later contracts, and Observe restores neutral. Rounded rim no longer forms flat membranes. Side/front/top and mouth/pouch focus are nonblank; source atlas grooves still form unnatural curves in some frontal regions. Regular relief, a simplified recessed oral back wall, stretched atlas marks and unmeasured wet optics remain. Aft-fin focus intentionally crops the forebody.
compiledReview.humpback: All 31 states inspected. Own dark/white atlas, tubercles and long pectorals retained; front pouch bows outward and contracts with unchanged trunk. Observe/swim/rest restore the same source skin. Mouth detail exposes coarse cheek/floor joins and simplified lining/baleen mats; no claim that these reproduce complete living oral anatomy. Pouch focus intentionally crops the tail.

beforeTargetRecords.summary: A baleen whale with long pectoral flippers. Feeding and breeding grounds are often separated by long migrations.

anatomy.name: Baleen
anatomy.description: Two selected upper-mouth baleen racks are visible during the feeding study. The display density, plate dimensions and fringe optics are authored; no prey capture or measured filtering efficiency.

anatomy.name: Pectoral flippers
anatomy.description: Long retained pectoral surfaces assist manoeuvring in real humpbacks. The neutral and local articulation studies do not fit measured flipper strokes or forces.

anatomy.name: Flukes
anatomy.description: Horizontal flukes and caudal body provide dorsoventral propulsion in life. During the authored lunge, tail posture changes toward the top of a beat near gape, then returns toward neutral; no fitted thrust.

anatomy.name: Ventral groove blubber and feeding pouch
anatomy.description: The retained pleated external surface expands beneath the mouth and anterior trunk, remains distended at lip closure, then contracts posteriorly and anteriorly. Pleat relief is mainly the creator atlas/normal image; tissue strain, pressure, tongue inversion and water transport are not resolved.

behaviors.label: Fluke and flipper study
behaviors.description: Retained Allie2k humpback surface with an independently authored dorsoventral tail-chain wave and gentle body/pectoral trim. This periodic local articulation is not a measured swimming trajectory, thrust, energetic model or complete motor controller.

rendering.reason: Local tail/pectoral articulation works; measured swimming trajectories, flow and force mechanisms remain unfinished.

behaviors.label: Lunge feeding study
behaviors.description: Finite exterior lunge-feeding study on the same credited skin: cranial elevation and mandibular depression open the oral seam, the ventral pouch expands, the mouth closes, and posterior then anterior pouch contraction illustrates slower draining. Paired authored baleen racks remain attached to the upper mouth. Selected dimensions, display plate density and timing are uncalibrated. Water flow, prey retention, tongue inversion, swallowing, respiration, forces and energetics are not simulated.
behaviors.evidence: Primary source-supported qualitative sequence; selected exterior geometry and timing, not fitted kinematics or physiological validation
behaviors.timeScale: Finite 35 uncalibrated authored seconds; no biological time calibration

rendering.reason: Working gape, retained outer pouch, paired baleen exteriors, closure and slower contraction stages. Fluid transport, food capture, tongue inversion and physiological filtration remain unfinished.

behaviors.label: Suspended neutral pose
behaviors.description: Inspect the same humpback at a static neutral suspension pose. This does not animate or infer sleep, breathing, buoyancy regulation or an experimentally established resting behaviour.

beforeTargetRecords.habitat: Marine pelagic waters and productive continental-shelf margins

beforeTargetRecords.summary: A large rorqual with a broad, relatively flat rostrum, mottled grey-blue skin, small posterior dorsal fin and horizontal flukes. Individual proportions and markings vary. The species-level accession does not identify the creator model to subspecies, sex, age or population.

anatomy.name: Broad rostrum and paired blowholes
anatomy.description: A broad, flatter selected dorsal rostrum with a median ridge and paired blowhole region. Head, eye and blowhole rims remain simplified; this is not an independently determined individual or subspecies.

anatomy.name: Horizontal flukes and caudal peduncle
anatomy.description: The retained horizontal flukes and tapering posterior body articulate dorsoventrally through the creator skeleton. Excursions, tissue strain and hydrodynamic performance have not been measured or fitted.

anatomy.name: Pectoral flippers and ventral pleats
anatomy.description: The compact retained pectorals and grey-blue pleated exterior remain on the same model. The feeding study distends that external ventral skin and closes the lips before slower pouch contraction. Pleat relief remains mainly source atlas/normal detail; dimensions, material strain, flow and pressure are unmeasured.

anatomy.name: Small posterior dorsal fin
anatomy.description: A low selected dorsal-fin exterior is retained near the posterior quarter of the body. Its smooth joined root follows the same skin. The reduced outline and relative height are authored choices, not a fit to a measured individual or universal fin dimensions.

Observe holds the first creator frame, avoiding a discontinuous switch from the raw bind pose.
